Video Highlights:
Theme: The song depicts the Saptarishi (the seven sages) attempting to reason with Goddess Parvati regarding her choice of Lord Shiva (Bholenath) as her husband (0:19-0:30).
The Sages' Concerns: The lyrics highlight the sages' bewilderment at Shiva's simple and unworldly lifestyle—contrasting his appearance (wearing snakes, having the Ganga on his head) with the traditional expectations of a groom (1:29-2:04).
Divine Contrast: The song celebrates the unique nature of Bholenath, describing him as a devotee of Ram, a conqueror of desire (Kaamdev), and someone who exists beyond typical household concerns (3:04-3:40).

text:
This is a super popular Bundelkhandi / Awadhi folk Shiv-Parvati song - it's the scene where Parvati is doing tapasya to marry Shiva, and Saptarishis come to convince her not to.

Here is the story line by line:

*Shambho, Shiva Shambho, Bholenath / Jab zid pe aa gayi Parvati Parvati*
- The song sets the scene - Parvati is adamant on marrying Shiva.

*Samjaane pahunche Saptarishi / Kaay zid kar rai, kaay ko mar rai, aise var ke laane*
- The 7 sages come to counsel her: "Why are you so stubborn, why are you killing yourself over _this kind_ of groom?"

*Jaake seesh pe Ganga aur gale mein daale phir rahe saanp / Itne seedhe saadhe hain sab kehte Bholenath*
- The one who has Ganga on his head and snakes around his neck - everyone calls him Bholenath because he's so simple/innocent.

*Na kapda na chhapra, na phoos ki dhare madaiya / Ka kaave ko dharo wahaan, bas rovat rahat ladaiya*
- He has no clothes, no roof, not even a straw hut / What will you do there? You'll just keep crying and fighting.

*Bhesh dhare avadhoot phire / Dora daangar le ghoome, ve inke kacchu e naiyya*
- He roams as an ascetic, an avadhoot / He roams with bull (Nandi) - he has no cattle or possessions.

This is the sages taunting Shiva's lifestyle to scare Parvati.

*Jata lata na kabahu sanwaare, deesat maha bhayankar / Moodh pe aadho chanda aur bela pe ghoome Shankar*
- He never combs his matted locks, looks very frightening / He has half-moon on his head and roams on cremation grounds (or with bull).

*Ram naam ke rasiya hain ve, aur unhein kya chaahne / Kaamdev ke mardanhaari, ghar grihasthi kya jaane*
- He is lost in chanting Ram's name, what desires does he have? / He is the destroyer of Kamdev (lust), what does he know of married household life?

*Kaay zid kar rai, kaay tap kar rai, aise var ke laane*
- Repeats - Why are you so stubborn, doing such penance for a groom like this?

The whole folk teases Shiva, but the hidden meaning is devotion - Parvati knows he is Bholenath, simple and pure, and that's exactly why she wants him.
